response:
It makes a lot of sense that dissociation became a coping tool—your mind did what it needed to protect you. Recognizing that it's no longer serving you is an important step. Grounding techniques can help you stay present: try naming things you see, hear, and feel around you, holding something cold, or focusing on slow breathing. Some people find it helpful to press their feet firmly into the floor or count backward from 100.

Because dissociation often stems from past experiences, working with a trauma-informed therapist can make a real difference. They can help you understand your triggers and develop tools that feel safe and manageable. Healing takes time, and you don't have to figure this out alone. If you ever feel overwhelmed or unsafe, please reach out to a crisis line or someone you trust.
